questions.question: What is a Copilot agent?
options: A scoped or focused version of Copilot that acts as an AI assistant and can automate business processes using web and work data
A standalone desktop app installed separately from Microsoft 365
A one-time prompt template that cannot access any data
A hardware device that runs Copilot locally
questions.explanation: An agent is a scoped version of Copilot, tailored to specific tasks or knowledge, that can automate processes and use web and work data (Microsoft Graph and Work IQ).

questions.question: How does the Researcher agent differ from standard Copilot chat?
options: It reasons more deeply across multiple sources and takes longer to produce a comprehensive, cited, shareable report
It is faster than standard chat for every task
It behaves identically to chat; only the name is different
It can only answer one-word questions
questions.explanation: Researcher is built for deeper reasoning across the web and your work content and deliberately takes longer to produce a thorough, cited report, whereas standard chat is optimized for speed and quick tasks.

questions.question: In Agent Builder, how can you create an agent?
options: Describe it in natural language and have Copilot build it, or configure it manually with a name, description, instructions, knowledge, and starter prompts
Only by writing code in a developer IDE
Only by copying someone else's existing agent
By recording a macro of your clicks
questions.explanation: Agent Builder lets you describe the agent in natural language (recommended) or configure it manually on the Configure tab, setting its name, description, instructions, knowledge, and starter prompts.

questions.question: What are starter prompts in an agent for?
options: To help other users understand the scenarios the agent commonly supports
To set the agent's billing limits
To permanently lock the agent's instructions
To translate the agent into other languages
questions.explanation: Starter prompts help users understand what an agent can do by showing common scenarios it supports; each has a name and a description.

questions.question: Select all the knowledge sources an agent built in Agent Builder can use.
options: Public websites
SharePoint and OneDrive content
Teams chats and meetings
Outlook email and uploaded (embedded) files
The user's locally installed antivirus software
questions.explanation: Agent Builder supports knowledge sources such as public websites, SharePoint and OneDrive, Teams chats and meetings, Outlook email, embedded files, and Copilot connectors. Antivirus software is not a knowledge source.

questions.question: Select everything a Researcher agent response is designed to include.
options: Visuals, charts, and graphs
Organized sections
Cited sources
An audio narration of the report
A live, editable spreadsheet
questions.explanation: A Researcher response is designed to include visuals and charts, organized sections, and cited sources. It does not produce an audio narration or a live editable spreadsheet.
